title: Irrigation Billing Q&A — Lines Credited against the Electric Service by Rate Schedule Seasonal Minimum
content:
These answers set out which billed lines of an Electric Service by Rate Schedule irrigation account count against its seasonal minimum. The test is the number of billing periods of the settlement's twelve months — lines dated less than twelve whole months before the current date — in which demand charge lines stand.

**A short season: demand charge lines in one, two or three billing periods.** A short pumping season's demand charges recover their own demand-related cost, so only the facility and energy charge lines are credited.

**Demand charge lines in four, five or six billing periods.** The facility and energy charge lines and half of the demand charge lines, that half rounded to the cent, are credited.

**Any other case** — no demand charge line, or demand charge lines in seven or more billing periods. The facility, energy and demand charge lines are credited.

### Credited lines at a glance

| Billing periods with demand charge lines | Credited |
|---|---|
| 1 to 3 | Facility and energy lines |
| 4 to 6 | Facility and energy lines, and half the demand lines |
| 0, or 7 or more | Facility, energy and demand lines |

### Hypothetical worked case

Lines of the twelve months: facility $324.00, energy $2,180.45, demand $1,342.00.

| Periods with demand lines | Credited lines |
|---|---|
| 3 | $2,504.45 |
| 5 | $2,504.45 plus $671.00, $3,175.45 |
| 7 | $3,846.45 |
